articles.title: Madden review – Nicolas Cage is a cartoonish NFL legend in David O Russell’s stinker
articles.summary: Oscar-nominated director delivers a thoroughly unserious biopic, wasting Christian Bale and Sienna Miller’s talents. John Madden was a beloved American original, the burly football coach who segued easily from Super Bowl burnout to television darling to the last name in gaming as the NFL was…
body: That the Madden video game franchise outlived the avuncular Minnesotan, whose death at age 85 in 2021 was mourned throughout the sport, is as much a testament to his singular knack for teaching the game’s fundaments as it is to his willingness to bring his classroom to students, wherever they might huddle. But Madden, a new Amazon biopic that can’t decide whether it’s serious or slapstick, has drawn all the wrong lessons.

Mulaney knows the film he’s in is a stinker – and so, for that matter, does Miller. She looks like she might crack up at the ridiculousness in early scenes as Raiders first lady Carol Davis. But in her defense: it would be hard for anyone to keep a straight face opposite Bale – who more than justifies the makeup and costuming departments’ considerable efforts to revive Davis, the NFL’s immortal rogue. Bale nails Davis’s Brooklyn accent, the pimp swagger and his roiling insistence on being the smartest guy in the room – right down to diagnosing Madden’s persistent stomach problems as “gas”. Turns out, it was a bleeding ulcer.
points: Oscar-nominated director delivers a thoroughly unserious biopic, wasting Christian Bale and Sienna Miller’s talents.

articles.title: As U.S. Infrastructure Crumbles, ABC’s ‘World News Tonight’ Posts Highest Week-Long Daily Ratings Since COVID
articles.summary: A week after the midterm elections generated tremendous audiences for the network evening newscasts, last week’s unpredictable string of news — including the Microsoft Outlook blackout, followed by the nationwide grounding of air flights — propelled ABC’s “World News Tonight” to heights the…
body: According to ABC News, “World News Tonight” averaged more than 9 million Total Viewers on each of its five telecasts last week — the first time it has done that in nearly six years, during the COVID era (specifically, the week of Feb. 15, 2021).

“Audiences are turning to ‘World News Tonight with David Muir ’ in numbers we haven’t seen since the COVID pandemic, a powerful reflection of the trust they place in our journalism during uncertain times,” said ABC News president Almin Karamehmedovic in a statement to Variety. “Amid a relentless week of breaking news, culminating in Friday’s nationwide ground stop, more than 9 million Americans tuned in every single night. We are deeply grateful for their confidence and never take that responsibility for granted.”

articles.title: Zombucha! review – new Australian zombie film never quite finds its bite
articles.summary: An accident in kombucha brewing leads to a zombie outbreak in a movie which is a little too low-key to live up to its delicious potential. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. Zombucha! is a relatively rare example of a genre film that’s not really a genre film.
body: What we do get is an enjoyably staged and well-paced production that’s never boring, despite the long wait for the main action. There’s also something kind of endearing about a zombie film so low-key it almost forgets to be a zombie film. Emma Leonard’s writing, Claudia Dzienny’s direction and the performances are all appealing, albeit lacking some flair. I was consistently entertained but will probably never return for a rewatch.

Meanwhile, her husband, Leo (Ryan O’Kane), the creative director at an advertising agency, is getting great feedback from clients – his ad for an energy drink considered “poetic” and “paradigm-shifting”. But he’s tired of working crazy long hours for the “toxic capitalist machine”, despite some generous perks from his boss Hopper (Jackie van Beek), such as a bag of white powder to help him power through. So Leo quits his job, which Maddie isn’t thrilled about, given she lost hers on the same day and the pair are “mortgaged up to the freakin’ eyeballs”.
points: An accident in kombucha brewing leads to a zombie outbreak in a movie which is a little too low-key to live up to its delicious potential.
Zombucha! is a relatively rare example of a genre film that’s not really a genre film.

articles.title: Josephine review – Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan ballast knotty drama about a child witness to a rape
articles.summary: Mason Reeves steals the show as an eight year old who stumbles across a sex assault but, despite strong performances, parts of the film feel contrived. Beth de Araújo’s new movie takes a very big swing, and it has won prizes and acclaim since its premiere at Sundance.
body: Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan play Damien and Claire, a smart professional couple in San Francisco with a bright young daughter called Josephine, marvellously played by Reeves. Damien takes Josephine to Golden Gate Park one morning to play football (they turn out to enjoy watching the English Premier League on TV). She mischievously runs on ahead of her dad to a secluded spot in the park where Damien can’t immediately find her and it is there that Josephine witnesses a rape – not less horrifying for being filmed in long shot.

Damien catches up with Josephine, and gives chase to the rapist; Josephine and the rape victim find themselves in the back of a police car while the cops and Damien deal with matters, almost as if they are culprits and prisoners. Deeply affected by something she cannot understand or process in her mind, Josephine starts acting out in school, not helped by Damien bizarrely insisting she take self-defence classes. Her disorientation borders on psychosis, and all the time the court date nears when Josephine has to give evidence in front of a jury.
points: Mason Reeves steals the show as an eight year old who stumbles across a sex assault but, despite strong performances, parts of the film feel contrived.
Beth de Araújo’s new movie takes a very big swing, and it has won prizes and acclaim since its premiere at Sundance.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics
articles.summary: Critics have their say as to whether GTA 6, the most anticipated video game of all time, lives up to the hype.
body: After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at 99 out of 100, external - tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.
Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.

articles.title: Rose Byrne on What Lured Her to ‘The Good Daughter’ and Why That Complicated Ending Wraps the Series
articles.summary: The star and executive producer unpacks the thrilling Peacock mystery also starring Meghann Fahy and if what happens to the young girl at the center of it is fair.
body: Rose Byrne keeps outdoing herself. Her explosive limited series The Good Daughter co-starring Meghann Fahy quickly became the top show on Peacock. Just last year, she grabbed a best actress Oscar nomination and won both the Golden Globe and Independent Spirits Award for If I Had Legs I’d Kick You — the film nobody saw coming. She also wrapped season two of her Apple TV comedy Platonic.

It’s the kind of story that Byrne, who also serves as executive producer alongside fellow Aussie, Big Little Lies Emmy winner Bruna Papandrea, sees as bestselling author and fellow EP Karin Slaughter’s superpower. “She writes incredibly rich female characters who are complicated and complex, and not all good and not all bad, and who have a lot to work with,” Byrne continued.

articles.title: Julio Iglesias facing court investigation over alleged sexual offences
articles.summary: The 83-year-old singer is accused of abusing two former employees at Caribbean residences in 2021.
body: Two women, who worked for the 83-year-old in the Caribbean, have accused him of abuse which they say took place in the Bahamas and the Dominican Republic in 2021.
The announcement comes after Spanish prosecutors dropped an inquiry into the claims earlier this year after concluding that they lacked jurisdiction because the alleged crimes took place abroad.
Iglesias, who has been a household name in Spain since the 1960s and has sold millions of records worldwide, has previously denied the allegations.

But in a statement published on Wednesday, external (in Spanish), national court Judge Antonio Piña said the account given in the complaint, alongside preliminary evidence provided, justified opening criminal proceedings.
